All 46 tests ran, with exactly 1 failure confirming the real bug found during probing. 45 pass, 1 fails for the expected reason.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/StringEscapeUtilsAgentTest.java` with 46 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering null/empty handling, Java/EcmaScript/JSON escaping differences, HTML3 vs HTML4 entity support, XML 1.0/1.1 control-character handling, CSV escaping/unescaping, and round-trips.

**One test fails, revealing a real bug:**

- `testUnescapeCsvSingleQuoteCharacterDoesNotThrow` — `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeCsv("\"")` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning the input unchanged. In `CsvUnescaper.translate`, when the single-character input is itself the quote character, both `charAt(0)` and `charAt(length-1)` resolve to the same character, so the code wrongly treats it as "enclosed in quotes" and calls `input.subSequence(1, input.length() - 1)`, i.e. `subSequence(1, 0)`, which is an invalid range and throws. All 45 other tests pass.
